settings.title: Worldwide Contact System
settings.strapline: Connect people and practical work across places and cultures.

pages.heading: Find a route into every place.
pages.body: A contact workbench for GAJRA Earth, P4A and the Web3 Sensorium. Explore existing networks, connect useful work to local needs and prepare a relevant introduction.

pages.heading: Start with an existing connection.
pages.body: Find public directories and organisations that can open a conversation. Check the local organisation and choose the appropriate contact route.

pages.heading: Every place has its own context.
pages.body: Explore the country and territory reference list. Record real connections as they develop, while making room for communities that cross borders.

pages.heading: Useful work gives an invitation substance.
pages.body: Approach people through a subject that matters locally. These connected projects offer several ways to begin.

pages.heading: Prepare a relevant introduction.
pages.body: Choose the place, project and request. Make the wording your own, then decide how to share it.

pages.heading: Make contact. Keep the next step clear.
pages.body: A repeatable way to find appropriate people, make a useful approach and turn replies into direct relationships.

pages.heading: Keep the working records together.
pages.body: Edit public website content in the CMS. Keep personal contacts, correspondence and outreach decisions in the private workspace.

projects.title: Your Relevance in every jurisdiction
projects.summary: Adapt the method of investigating the rules affecting a person's own circumstances to the sources, jurisdictions and choices relevant in each place.
projects.invite: Discuss a locally grounded adaptation of Your Relevance, or introduce people interested in legal understanding and informed civic participation.

projects.title: Australian Legal Engine
projects.summary: Retrieve and quote provisions from locally indexed Australian legislation, with source addresses and dates. Follow connections between acts and bring the original text into a legal research conversation.
projects.invite: Discuss source-grounded legal research, locally held legislation and ways to make relevant provisions easier to find and check.

projects.title: Installing the Missing Middle
projects.summary: Develop community-scale computing with useful heat, resilient power, workforce learning and a pathway to local ownership. Personal and community data authority remains part of the design.
projects.invite: Explore a place-specific conversation about community computing, locally useful workloads, installation capability and data authority.

projects.title: P4A Australia
projects.summary: Explore civic participation through local places, everyday issues, public evidence and connected proposals for Australia's future.
projects.invite: Discuss relevant local civic or cultural questions, suggest a source, or introduce interested residents and community organisations.

projects.title: P4A Oceania
projects.summary: Explore how P4A's civic workbench could translate across Oceania, with local contexts, regional connections and questions shaped by the people who live there.
projects.invite: Introduce interested residents or local organisations to discuss civic participation, regional connections and locally relevant ideas across Oceania.

projects.title: P4A Native Nations
projects.summary: Explore Indigenous nations, treaties, knowledge and data sovereignty, with participation and locally chosen pathways grounded in each nation's own authority.
projects.invite: Discuss an appropriate introduction or locally chosen contribution, with the relevant Indigenous people determining the scope and sharing of their knowledge.

projects.title: GAJRA Earth Infinity
projects.summary: A public presentation of Joyful Responsible Abundance as living practice, with local interpretation, reflection, contribution and connections across cultures.
projects.invite: Connect with Luke about locally meaningful participation, language and cultural perspectives, or practical work that people choose to develop together.

projects.title: GAJRA Earth Claude
projects.summary: Explore the Claude-built GAJRA Earth invitation: Joyful Responsible Abundance, human and AI alignment, and questions people can help define across cultures.
projects.invite: Invite a conversation about Joyful Responsible Abundance, public questions and locally meaningful contributions to human and AI alignment.

projects.title: GAJRA Earth Community
projects.summary: Find starting points for shared action through GAJRA Earth's public hub: community contributions, events, travel, research and practical work towards Joyful Responsible Abundance.
projects.invite: Introduce a local interest, useful skill or community project and explore how people might contribute and share what they learn.

projects.title: Aura Genesis
projects.summary: Explore the Aura Genesis Protocol: developing personal intelligence through a digital twin of body and mind, reflective learning and the proposed Genesis process.
projects.invite: Discuss personal intelligence, reflective learning and a locally relevant starting point for exploring the Aura Genesis proposal.

projects.title: Aura Tourism
projects.summary: Explore personal intelligence through travel, music, sport, culture, nature and reflection, beginning on Minjerribah and connecting with wider tourism and learning opportunities.
projects.invite: Discuss a tourism or community learning opportunity that connects enjoyable experiences, local knowledge and personal intelligence.

projects.title: Aura Disaster Resilience
projects.summary: Connect everyday community capability with location-specific preparedness, communications, practical learning and continuing recovery.
projects.invite: Discuss local hazards, community knowledge and practical preparedness or recovery work, and identify interested local contributors.

projects.title: Aura Children & Young People
projects.summary: Explore a proposal for children and young people in Australian care, beginning with chosen interests and supported creative learning. Connect self-understanding, rights, family, culture and mentoring with opportunities for adulthood.
projects.invite: Discuss supported creative learning, mentoring or a locally relevant introduction for exploring the children and young people's Aura proposal.

projects.title: Aura Whole-of-Life Support
projects.summary: Explore proposed personal-intelligence support for adults living with dementia or disability, people beginning aged care and their supporters. Connect memory, personal context and everyday choices with human-directed support.
projects.invite: Discuss an everyday support need, a potential research or service partnership, or an introduction to supporters interested in the whole-of-life proposal.

projects.title: Verse Box
projects.summary: Explore a proposed portable introduction to Aura of Intelligence: personal Aura building, learning, Community Hours and civic participation using lower-cost equipment.
projects.invite: Explore a locally useful public demonstration, a possible host setting or a contribution to personal Aura learning and community participation.

projects.title: A fair go in the age of intelligence
projects.summary: Luke's UNGA81 contribution invites locally shaped cooperation around Joyful Responsible Abundance, meaningful choices and useful capability shared between places.
projects.invite: Circulate the invitation or discuss how locally rooted associations could cooperate across countries and cultures while retaining their own judgment.

projects.title: Joyful Responsible Abundance
projects.summary: Explore how personal intelligence, community capability, sovereign compute and civic participation connect in a whole-system proposal for Joyful Responsible Abundance, with source papers and tools for considering Australian choices in the age of superintelligence.
projects.invite: Discuss a locally meaningful starting point for Joyful Responsible Abundance, or connect a community interest with the proposal's practical tools and source papers.

projects.title: Mutual Futures
projects.summary: Explore shared ownership, business succession, learning, care and time through the AI transition. Connect productive technology with local capability, livelihoods and opportunities people can help shape.
projects.invite: Introduce a business handover, community need, useful skill or shared-ownership idea and explore a practical contribution to Mutual Futures.

sources.name: Grassroots Justice Network
sources.summary: An organisation directory for discovering legal empowerment groups. Listings are crowdsourced and require verification.
sources.contact_route: Use the organisation listing to identify its own public website or appropriate organisational enquiry route. Do not harvest member personal details.

sources.name: GNDR
sources.summary: A directory of civil society organisations working on disaster reduction and community resilience, with routes to national focal points.
sources.contact_route: Find an organisation or national focal point, verify its current public contact route, then enquire about an introduction or appropriate circulation.

sources.name: Association for Progressive Communications
sources.summary: A network of organisations working on community technology, communications, digital rights and local capability.
sources.contact_route: Follow the Members route from APC's own site and approach a relevant organisation through its published contact channel.

sources.name: Internet Society chapters
sources.summary: A chapter directory with public websites and contact emails for local Internet-related work.
sources.contact_route: Choose the relevant chapter, check its website and published organisational contact, and ask about community technology connections.

sources.name: Asia Indigenous Peoples Pact
sources.summary: A regional network of Indigenous peoples' organisations. Its own public site provides a route to the regional organisation.
sources.contact_route: Ask the regional organisation or an identified member's own public contact how to make a relevant invitation available.

sources.name: Indigenous Peoples of Africa Co-ordinating Committee
sources.summary: An African network of Indigenous peoples' organisations with a public member-organisation map.
sources.contact_route: Use the member map or published regional contact to identify an appropriate organisational introduction.

sources.name: Global Voices and Rising Voices
sources.summary: Public routes into a community of writers, translators and participatory media practitioners, including work with underrepresented language communities.
sources.contact_route: Follow contributor, Rising Voices or partnership routes and approach the appropriate published organisational contact.

sources.name: Wikimedia affiliates and user groups
sources.summary: A directory of geographic, thematic and language-related affiliates, including groups with established contact people.
sources.contact_route: Read the relevant group page and use its stated contact or discussion channel for a suitable introduction.

sources.name: URI Cooperation Circles
sources.summary: A searchable directory of community-led groups working across cultures, faiths and traditions.
sources.contact_route: Search by region, country or subject, read the group's own description, and use its published contact route.

sources.name: WFUNA national associations
sources.summary: A public directory of national United Nations Associations and organisational contact routes.
sources.contact_route: Identify a relevant national association and approach its published office contact about circulation or a conversation.

sources.name: Rotary and Rotaract clubs
sources.summary: An entry route to service clubs, local organisers and the connected Rotary and Rotaract networks.
sources.contact_route: Use the club-finding routes and a club's own public contact details to ask about an appropriate introduction or circulation.

sources.name: Toastmasters club finder
sources.summary: A club finder with routes to message club officers and identify meetings suitable for English communication.
sources.contact_route: Select a relevant open club, confirm its meeting language, and enquire through its listed officer-contact route.

sources.name: Servas groups
sources.summary: A directory of national and regional Servas group websites and social pages where provided.
sources.contact_route: Use the relevant group's own published contact route to enquire about English-speaking residents and suitable introductions.

sources.name: TESOL affiliate associations
sources.summary: An affiliate directory connecting national and regional English-language teaching associations.
sources.contact_route: Follow an association's own website and contact its organising committee about a relevant invitation or introduction.

sources.name: IATEFL teaching associations
sources.summary: An entry route to national and regional teaching associations within IATEFL's associate network.
sources.contact_route: Identify the appropriate association, verify its own contact details and ask about a relevant circulation or introduction.

sources.name: Co-operative and local trade networks
sources.summary: Use the ICA member directory as one research route to co-operative organisations. Find local trade and professional groups separately for the particular place.
sources.contact_route: Identify a relevant organisation, verify its own public contact and local relevance, and ask about community capability or practical introductions.
